chunks: And towards the three who were left behind, until when the earth, with all its expanse, became narrow for them and their souls were confined, and they thought that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him, then He relented towards them so that they may repent; surely Allah is the Accepter of Repentance, the Merciful.
ai.seo_question: Who were the three companions left behind in the Battle of the Ditch and how did Allah accept their repentance?
ai.summary: While the verse explicitly mentions three individuals, Shia exegetes such as Al-Tabarsi and Al-Kulayni identify them as Ka'b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayyah, who lagged behind during the Expedition of Tabuk rather than the Battle of the Ditch. The narrative highlights the psychological weight of their guilt, where the vastness of the earth felt narrow, leading to a sincere repentance (tawbah) that underscores Allah's attribute as Al-Tawwab. This event serves as a paradigm for the acceptance of repentance even after a period of concealment, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the continuity of divine mercy for the faithful.
